zh.thesis: 每个网站都塞满弹窗和横幅，是因为我们一边咒骂一边习惯，而法律和商业规则也为此开了绿灯。
paragraphs: 打开任何一个网页，先弹出来的是「我们用了 Cookie」的警告，旁边还跟着订阅框和优惠码。关掉一个，另一个又冒出来。
这篇文章把这种体验拆开看：COVID 提示、弹窗广告、邮件订阅、聊天机器人、页脚的一长串链接，每个都像约定俗成，但每个都让人烦。
为什么没人制止？作者说，法律要网站告诉你它用了 Cookie，于是就有了无处不在的横幅，但没人管它是否碍事。
商业上，优惠码和订阅框能带来转化，网站宁可牺牲体验也要多抓几个用户。机器人客服是装样子，真正的问题没人解决。
更深一层，用户其实有责任。我们嘴上骂，但手还是点了「我同意」，填了邮箱，用了优惠码。抱怨和行动互相矛盾。
结果就是，这一切成了一场比赛：看谁先适应对方的套路。网站赢，因为它的弹窗是精心设计的；你赢不了，因为你只有关闭按钮。
所以这篇的结论很悲观：这种混乱不是 bug，是每个人的选择叠加成的「特性」。只要有人点、有人买，弹窗就永远关不掉。

en.thesis: Every website is stuffed with pop-ups and banners because we curse at them even as we get used to them, and the law and business rules have given them the green light.
paragraphs: Open any webpage and the first thing that pops up is a warning that says 'we use cookies', with a subscription box and a discount code right next to it. Close one, and another appears.

This article takes that experience apart: the COVID notice, the pop-up ad, the email sign-up, the chat bot, the long line of links in the footer — each one feels like a convention, and each one annoys.
Why does nobody stop it? The author says the law requires websites to tell you they use cookies, so banners are everywhere, but nobody cares whether they get in the way.

On the business side, discount codes and subscription boxes bring conversions, so sites would rather hurt the experience than miss a few users. The chat bots are just for show; the real problems go unsolved.
Digging deeper, the user shares the blame. We complain out loud, but our hands still click 'I agree', fill in the email, and use the code. The grumbling and the action contradict each other.
The result is that it all becomes a game of who adapts to whose tricks first. The site wins because its pop-up is carefully designed; you lose because all you have is the close button.
So the article ends on a bleak note: this mess is not a bug, it is a 'feature' built out of everyone's choices. As long as someone clicks and someone buys, the pop-ups will never go away.

articles.title: The Economics of a Shrinking World
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 全球生育率下降已不可逆，且集中在穷国和低教育女性，后果是经济增长持续放缓。
paragraphs: 2026 年，人类整体生育率可能低于更替水平。这在历史上从未发生过，战争和瘟疫都没做到过。
但真正的意外是，生育率暴跌集中在低收入和中收入国家，尤其是穷的、教育程度低的女性。
研究者用单因子模型拟合了 236 个国家 1950 年以来的数据。共同因子在 1978 年见顶，之后一路下滑，如今拖累各国的是各自独有的趋势，219 个负数，没有一个在回升。
常见的解释都说不通，他们提出一个猜想：是现代性本身。它让生第三个孩子变得昂贵，让不生变得廉价。
孩子只能按整数生，所以一点小变化就能把生育率从 1.8 推到 1.3。而经济体系里没有任何力量会把生育率推回 2.1。
后果主要是增长放缓。人少了，劳动力、创新、需求都会跟着缩，经济这台机器转得就慢。
但 Cowen 补了一句：共同因子的峰值在 1978 年，那正好是避孕药普及的时间点。所谓现代性，说到底可能还是生育控制。

en.thesis: Global fertility decline is irreversible and concentrated in poor and low-educated women, with the consequence of sustained economic slowdown.
paragraphs: In 2026, overall human fertility may fall below replacement level. That has never happened before; even wars and plagues did not do it.
But the real surprise is that the fertility crash is concentrated in low- and middle-income countries, especially among poor, poorly educated women.

Researchers fit a single-factor model to data from 236 countries since 1950. The common factor peaked in 1978 and has been sliding ever since. What drags each country down now is its own unique trend: 219 are negative, and none are recovering.
Common explanations do not hold up. They propose a guess: it is modernity itself. Modernity makes having a third child expensive and makes not having one cheap.
Children come only in whole numbers, so a small change can push fertility from 1.8 down to 1.3. And no force in the economic system will push it back up to 2.1.
The consequence is mainly slower growth. Fewer people means labor, innovation, and demand all shrink, so the economic machine turns more slowly.
But Cowen adds a footnote: the common factor peaked in 1978, exactly when the pill became widespread. What we call modernity, in the end, may just be birth control.

articles.title: History often hinges on boring technical questions
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: 宏观经济的技术细节决定选举结果，却总被忽视。
paragraphs: 本文借读者提问讨论一个观点：许多历史转折点，背后其实是被忽略的货币政策细节。
比如 1874 年格兰特否决通货膨胀法案，若他签署，经济复苏可能更快，民主党就不会大胜，1876 年选举争议或可避免，重建时期或许延续更久。
但作者也承认，学界对法案效果有分歧，弗里德曼认为关键在于 1873 年的铸币法案，而非通胀法案。
更典型的是希特勒的崛起。1928 年经济稳定时纳粹仅得 2.6% 选票，大萧条后迅速升至第二，若当时德国应对经济危机更有效，纳粹可能不会上台。
2016 年特朗普当选也与之相似。作者认为，若美联储在通胀低于 2% 时不提前紧缩，希拉里或能险胜。
因此，宏观政策的技术细节常被舆论忽略，却对短期经济与选举结果至关重要。
作者认为，这些细节虽枯燥，却是政治中最被低估的因素。

en.thesis: Macroeconomic technical details decide elections, yet they are often ignored.
paragraphs: This article, prompted by a reader's question, discusses an idea: many turning points in history hide behind neglected details of monetary policy.

For example, in 1874 Grant vetoed the inflation bill. Had he signed it, the economy might have recovered faster, the Democrats would not have won big, the disputed 1876 election could have been avoided, and Reconstruction might have lasted longer.
But the author admits scholars disagree on the bill's effect. Friedman thought the key was the Coinage Act of 1873, not the inflation bill.

More typical is Hitler's rise. In 1928, with economic stability, the Nazis got only 2.6% of the vote. After the Depression they quickly became the second party. Had Germany coped with the crisis more effectively, the Nazis might never have come to power.
Trump's victory in 2016 is similar. The author argues that if the Fed had not tightened prematurely when inflation was below 2%, Clinton might have narrowly won.
So the technical details of macro policy are often overlooked by public opinion, yet they matter greatly for the short-term economy and election outcomes.
The author concludes that while these details are dull, they are the most underestimated factor in politics.

articles.title: Regulated Markets Are Slow to Handle Change
articles.author: Alex Tabarrok

zh.thesis: 为了证明电厂还有用，受监管的电力公司宁可亏本烧煤，也不肯转向便宜的天燃气。
paragraphs: 美国电力行业曾经是自然垄断，所以政府管价格。怎么定合理价格？不好说，于是允许电力公司回收运营成本，外加资本金的一定回报。
利润和资本金挂钩，公司就有动力多建电厂，这就是经典的 Averch-Johnson 效应。监管者于是规定，资本必须「被使用且有用」。
在稳定年代，这条规则能防止过度建设。但天燃气发电成本大跌之后，麻烦来了。
自由市场里，煤电不赚钱就该关停。可受监管的公司不能随便放弃，否则资本金就白投了。
于是它们继续烧煤，向监管者证明电厂还有用。就算烧煤的成本超过电价，也要硬着头皮烧。
数据证实了这一点。市场化改革后的州，煤价贵时立刻减少燃煤；受监管的州反应迟钝得多。同一个州对气价却很敏感。
所以监管的本意是防止浪费，结果在技术变革期反而让旧技术苟延残喘，连新技术也过度建设。监管在静态世界里还能用，一遇上变化就失效了。

en.thesis: To prove their plants are still useful, regulated power companies would rather lose money burning coal than switch to cheaper natural gas.
paragraphs: The American electricity industry used to be a natural monopoly, so the government controlled prices. How do you set a fair price? It is hard to say, so utilities were allowed to recover operating costs plus a certain return on their capital base.
When profits are tied to capital, companies have an incentive to build more plants. That is the classic Averch-Johnson effect. Regulators therefore required that capital be 'used and useful'.
In stable times, this rule prevents overbuilding. But trouble came when the cost of natural gas power generation plummeted.
In a free market, coal power that is not profitable should be shut down. But regulated companies cannot simply abandon it, or their capital investment is wasted.
So they keep burning coal to prove to regulators the plants are still useful. Even if the cost of burning coal exceeds the electricity price, they burn it anyway.

The data confirms this. In states that underwent market reform, coal use dropped immediately when coal prices rose; regulated states reacted much more slowly. The same states were very sensitive to gas prices.

So the intent of regulation was to prevent waste, but during technological change it instead lets old technologies linger on, and even overbuilds new ones. Regulation works in a static world, but fails when things change.

articles.title: 科技爱好者周刊（第 408 期）：你需要知道的 AI 缓存知识

zh.thesis: AI 缓存命中价便宜五十倍，所以提示词的顺序值得专门设计。
paragraphs: 大模型的收费分输入和输出两部分，这个好理解。但价目表上还有第三项，叫「输入缓存命中价」。很多人扫过去就跳过了，其实它是省钱的关键。
以 DeepSeek V4 Flash 为例，命中缓存一次只要 2 分钱，没命中是 1 元。差了整整五十倍。
为什么差这么多？模型要把提示词拆成 Token，再算它们两两之间的注意力，这一步最耗算力。命中缓存就不必重算了，收的其实只是存储费。
所以多轮对话最划算。每一轮都要把之前的内容重新提交一遍，而那段前缀是不变的，模型可以直接取上次的结果。
但缓存有期限。DeepSeek 是 10 分钟，Anthropic 只有 5 分钟，OpenAI 在 10 到 30 分钟之间逐步失效。过期就得从头算，价格跳回 1 元。
于是 AI 工具会定时发请求保活。以前的做法是每 30 秒一次，十分钟就发 20 个请求，这笔钱也不少。
所以保活其实不用那么密。既然最短的缓存期限也有 5 分钟，每 4 分钟发一次就够了。

en.thesis: AI cache hits are fifty times cheaper than misses, so the order of the prompt is worth designing.
paragraphs: Large model pricing splits into input and output parts, which is easy to understand. But there is a third item on the price list, called the 'input cache hit price'. Many people skip it when they see it, but it is the key to saving money.
Take DeepSeek V4 Flash as an example: a cache hit costs only 2 fen, while a miss costs 1 yuan. That is a full fifty times difference.

Why is there such a big difference? The model needs to split the prompt into tokens and then calculate the attention between each pair, which is the most computation-heavy step. If the cache is hit, there is no need to recompute; the fee is basically just storage.
So multi-turn conversations are the most cost-effective. Each turn resubmits all the previous content, and since that prefix remains unchanged, the model can directly reuse the last result.

But the cache has a time limit. DeepSeek keeps it for 10 minutes, Anthropic only 5 minutes, and OpenAI gradually expires between 10 and 30 minutes. After expiration, it has to be recomputed, and the price jumps back to 1 yuan.
Therefore, AI tools send periodic keep-alive requests. The old practice was every 30 seconds, which means 20 requests per 10 minutes, and that money also adds up.
So keep-alive doesn't need to be that frequent. Since the shortest cache duration is 5 minutes, sending a request once every 4 minutes is enough.

articles.title: Why does Opus 5 feel worse to work with?
articles.author: numeri

zh.thesis: Opus 5 变强了却更难用，因为训练目标选错了方向。
paragraphs: 作者和他认识的同事都觉得，Opus 5 用起来像降级，虽然它比 Opus 4.7 和 4.8 更强，甚至能比肩 Fable。
问题不在能力，而在行为方式。旧模型会在意图不明时停下来问，不随便假设，也不擅自改你的计划。Opus 5 不会。
所以用 Opus 5 得时刻盯着，像照顾小孩。作者说，这可能是 Anthropic 内部两股力量造成的。
一是想造出能自我改进、递归升级到 AGI 的 AI；二是追求在 benchmark 上拿高分。这两件事都导向同一个方向。
benchmark 的任务是自包含的，不需要问问题，答案就摆在那里。训练时选那些敢于假设的模型，得分就高。
但真实工作不是 benchmark。上下文、意图、预算限制根本写不全，总有模糊的地方。这时你需要它停下来问，而不是猜。
所以读者该记住：AI 的进步不只是能力，还包括它对模糊性的处理方式。能力强的模型不一定更适合真实工作。

en.thesis: Opus 5 got stronger but harder to use, because the training objective picked the wrong direction.
paragraphs: The author and colleagues he knows all feel that Opus 5 feels like a downgrade, even though it is stronger than Opus 4.7 and 4.8, and can even rival Fable.
The problem is not ability, but behavior. The old model would stop and ask when intent was unclear; it would not assume, and it would not unilaterally change your plans. Opus 5 does not do that.
So using Opus 5 means watching it constantly, like taking care of a child. The author says this might be caused by two forces inside Anthropic.
One is to build an AI that can self-improve and recursively upgrade to AGI; the other is to chase high scores on benchmarks. Both point in the same direction.
Benchmark tasks are self-contained; they do not require asking questions, the answer is right there. If you train a model that dares to assume, it scores well.
But real work is not a benchmark. Context, intent, budget constraints cannot be fully written down; there is always ambiguity. That is when you need it to stop and ask, not guess.
So readers should remember: AI progress is not just ability, but also how it handles ambiguity. A more capable model is not necessarily better suited for real work.

zh.thesis: 把「提高效率」本身当成爱好，会让人陷入不断更换工具的循环，反而什么也做不出来。
paragraphs: 作者认为，把「生产力」当成一种爱好是个陷阱。不断换系统、优化工具，看似无害，其实会把你困在无尽的工具更替里，永远写不出想写的东西。
那些整天谈「构建系统」的人，其实只是在「试吃」系统。每尝到一种新口味就宣布从此只吃它，直到下一个更香的冒出来。
作者把这些人叫作「生产力游客」——像旅行博主晒足迹一样晒自己的工具，却从不在一个地方停留足够久，去真正吸收点什么。
新系统带来的只是「没有问责的希望」：设置过程给你前进的错觉，每次优化都刺激多巴胺，直到它突然耗尽，然后你又奔向下一个开源 AI 工作流。
这个循环有固定剧本：发现时喊「这改变一切」，迁移时花几小时导数据，传道时逼朋友也来用，摩擦后怒骂「不可原谅」，最后在论坛发「再见世界」帖子，重新开始。
作者引用了 Peter Drucker 的话：我们混淆了「效率」和「效能」，前者是正确地做事，后者是做正确的事。没有比「高效地做不该做的事」更没用的了。
所以，如果一个工作流让你觉得无聊，那是好事——说明它退居背景，不再占用你的心智。好工具都无聊。真正要紧的只有一个指标：它是否让你产出了东西。

en.thesis: Treating 'productivity' as a hobby traps you in a cycle of switching tools, so you never actually produce anything.
paragraphs: The author argues that turning productivity into a hobby is a trap. Constantly switching systems and optimizing tools seems harmless, but it locks you into an endless cycle of tool swapping, and you never write what you wanted to write.

People who talk all day about 'building systems' are really just 'tasting' systems. Every time a new flavor shows up, they declare they'll only eat that from now on, until the next, even fancier one appears.
The author calls these people 'productivity tourists' — they show off their tools like travel bloggers show off footprints, but they never stay in one place long enough to actually absorb something.

A new system only offers 'hope without accountability': the setup process gives you the illusion of progress, each optimization spikes your dopamine, until it suddenly fades, and then you dash off to the next open-source AI workflow.

This cycle follows a fixed script: when you discover it, you shout 'this changes everything'; when migrating, you spend hours importing data; when preaching, you force friends to try it; when friction hits, you curse 'unforgivable'; and finally you post a 'goodbye world' thread on a forum, then start over.

The author quotes Peter Drucker: we confuse 'efficiency' with 'effectiveness'. Efficiency is doing things right, effectiveness is doing the right things. Nothing is more useless than to do efficiently what should not be done at all.

So if a workflow feels boring, that's a good sign — it means it has receded into the background and no longer occupies your mind. Good tools are boring. The only metric that really matters is: does it get you to produce something?

articles.title: 3 myths about coding with AI that even experienced developers still believe
articles.author: Abhinav Raj

zh.thesis: AI 编程助手让程序员写代码的时间少了，但花在验证和纠错上的时间更多了。
paragraphs: AI 编程已经普及，但关于它的三个迷思仍然存在，连资深开发者都信。每个迷思背后都有研究和事实可以澄清。
第一个迷思是「AI 让开发者更高效」。奥克兰大学的研究显示，82% 的工程师写代码时间减少，但工作重心转向了验证和纠正 AI 的输出。
同时，声称开发体验变差的工程师比例从 14% 翻倍到 27%，尤其是在心流和认知负荷方面。写代码少了，不代表活少了。
第二个迷思是「AI 代码审查能发现人类漏掉的问题」。但 2025 年 9 月的研究测试了 GitHub Copilot 的审查功能，它经常漏掉 SQL 注入、跨站脚本等严重漏洞。
Copilot 反而把重点放在代码风格和拼写错误上。作者强调必须保留人工代码审计，不能完全依赖 AI。
第三个迷思是「AI 编程不过是高级自动补全」。但实际上，Claude Code 和 Codex 这样的工具能自主完成任务。在 Epoch AI 的基准中，Claude Opus 4.6 用 1.6 万行 Go 代码重写了生物信息学工具包。
所以，AI 编程的实际情况比传言复杂：它确实强大，但好处不是自动来的。用 AI 省下的时间，得再花在检查 AI 的工作上。

en.thesis: AI programming assistants cut the time programmers spend writing code, but they add time spent verifying and fixing it.
paragraphs: AI programming is everywhere, but three myths about it persist, and even experienced developers believe them. Each myth has research and facts that can clear it up.

The first myth is that AI makes developers more productive. Research from the University of Auckland shows that 82% of engineers spend less time writing code, but their work shifts to verifying and correcting AI output.
Meanwhile, the share of engineers who say the developer experience has worsened doubled from 14% to 27%, especially around flow and cognitive load. Writing less code does not mean less work.

The second myth is that AI code review catches problems humans miss. But a September 2025 study tested GitHub Copilot's review feature, and it often missed serious vulnerabilities like SQL injection and cross-site scripting.
Copilot instead focused on code style and spelling mistakes. The authors insist that human code review must stay, because you cannot rely on AI alone.

The third myth is that AI programming is just advanced autocomplete. But in reality, tools like Claude Code and Codex can finish tasks on their own. On Epoch AI's benchmark, Claude Opus 4.6 rewrote a bioinformatics toolkit in 16,000 lines of Go.

So the real picture of AI programming is more complicated than the rumors: it is powerful, sure, but the benefits do not come automatically. The time you save with AI, you have to spend checking AI's work.

articles.title: I trusted Antigravity and a local LLM with the same office tasks, and only one respected my files
articles.author: Nolen Jonker

zh.thesis: 文件型 AI 代理的差别不在能不能完成任务，而在它是否先读懂文件夹的结构再动手。
paragraphs: 聊天机器人说错话只是烦人，可一旦让 AI 直接操作你的文件，出错就真的要命。作者拿自己的 Obsidian 笔记库做测试，专门比了两类工具：谷歌的 Antigravity 和本地的 Qwen 3.5 9B。
先给它们各一篇杂乱的会议记录，要求整理格式、加摘要和行动项。两个都做完了，Antigravity 的归类更聪明，本地模型是机械式的，但基本都合格。
第二项是跨越五篇笔记做综合提炼。Antigravity 找出贯穿所有笔记的四个论点，本地模型虽然也给出四个主题，但更像逐篇的摘要，没有真跨笔记。差距开始显现。
关键测试是让它们新建一篇关于「标签与文件夹结构」的笔记，并放进合适的文件夹。Antigravity 先翻看了三个文件夹，选中 "notes/ux"，还沿用现有命名、格式，甚至主动加了链接。
本地模型虽然也找到了文件夹，但过程多绕弯，一开始还把我常用的笔记误归为「孤儿」，最后才修正。它不确定时倾向于写到根目录。
接着让它们往已有的 MOC 索引里加条目。Antigravity 主动阅读周边格式，新增内容与旧条目风格一致；本地模型找到了文件，却因为「已经改过」而没动手 —— 这倒是它最谨慎的一次。
两个工具都完成了任务，但作者在意的是它们如何对待文件夹。Antigravity 每次动手前都先读，本地模型偶尔也会犹豫。结论是：我会把重要的文件夹交给 Antigravity，它更体贴。

en.thesis: The difference between file-handling AI agents is not whether they finish the task but whether they figure out the folder structure before they start.
paragraphs: A chatbot that gets something wrong is just annoying. But once you let an AI work directly with your files, a mistake can be serious. The author tested two kinds of tools on his own Obsidian notes: Google's Antigravity and a local Qwen 3.5 9B.

First he gave each a messy meeting transcript and asked for formatting, a summary, and action items. Both finished the job. Antigravity sorted things more cleverly, and the local model was more mechanical, but both passed.

The second task was to synthesize across five notes. Antigravity found four arguments that ran through all of them. The local model also gave four themes, but they read like a summary of each note in turn, without true cross-note synthesis. The gap started to show.

The key test was asking them to create a new note about 'tags and folder structure' and put it in the right folder. Antigravity first browsed three folders, picked 'notes/ux', followed the existing naming and formatting, and even added links on its own.

The local model did find the folder, but it took a winding path. At first it misclassified one of my common notes as an 'orphan' and only corrected itself later. When it was unsure, it tended to write to the root directory.

Then he asked them to add an entry to an existing MOC index. Antigravity read the surrounding format and matched the style of the old entries. The local model found the file but did not touch it because it had 'already been modified' — which was, oddly, its most cautious moment.

Both tools completed the tasks. But what mattered to the author was how they treated the folder. Antigravity read first before every action, and the local model hesitated sometimes. Conclusion: for important folders, I would hand them to Antigravity — it is more considerate.

articles.title: Orwell: “It is possible to be a normal decent person and yet be fully alive.”
articles.author: conversableeconomist

zh.thesis: 正常而体面的人，也可以活得充实而完整。
paragraphs: 有个常见的说法：艺术家要活得狂野，最好英年早逝。酗酒、滥交、背叛，好像这样才算真正活过。反过来，一个踏实的丈夫和父亲，住在郊区当编辑，就被认为活得很没劲。
还有一种版本，把「全情投入」奉为最高。为了一个执念牺牲一切，这种偏执也被当作活生生的证据。
但经济学家会问：值不值？登山者死在峰顶，也许他本来就愿意用命换这次攀登。可我们这些不愿这么干的人，也因此活得更不完整吗？
Orwell 在 1936 年的书评里说过一句好话：「做一个正常体面的人，同时充分活着，这是可能的。」他认为，那种靠酗酒、纵欲来「逃避」的生活方式，其实是最糟的。
关键是别把「正常」「体面」当作贬义词。Orwell 不是在说只有这种人才配充分活着，他只是把一个看似矛盾的可能性顶了回来：普通人也能活出密度。
奇怪的是，21 世纪的很多人对这个说法本能地反感。好像非要打破常规、付出代价，才算没白活。
Orwell 留下的是另一种答案：不需要自我摧毁，日常本身就可以是完整的。抓住这一点，像抓住救生圈。

en.thesis: A normal and decent person can live a full and complete life.
paragraphs: There is a common saying: artists must live wildly and preferably die young. Drinking, promiscuity, betrayal — as if that is the only way to truly live. By contrast, a steady husband and father who lives in the suburbs and works as an editor is considered dull.
Another version elevates 'total commitment' as the highest ideal. Sacrificing everything for an obsession — that kind of zeal is also taken as proof of being alive.

But economists would ask: is it worth it? A climber who dies on the summit may have been willing to trade his life for that climb. But does that mean those of us who would not do that are living less fully?

Orwell said something good in a 1936 review: 'It is possible to be a normal decent person and yet be fully alive.' He thought that the lifestyle of 'escaping' through drink and lust was actually the worst.

The key is not to treat 'normal' and 'decent' as insults. Orwell wasn't saying only such people deserve to live fully; he was pushing back against a seeming contradiction: ordinary people can also live with intensity.
Strangely, many people in the 21st century instinctively recoil at this. As if you must break rules and pay a price to prove your life was not wasted.
Orwell offers a different answer: you don't need self-destruction; daily life itself can be complete. Hold on to that like a lifebuoy.

articles.title: Intergenerational mobility of immigrants in 15 destination countries
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 移民子女的收入差距一半来自父母收入，另一半来自目的地国家的劳动力市场和移民政策。
paragraphs: 这项研究比较了 15 个接收国里移民子女与本地人子女的收入。发现移民子女的收入要低一些。
差距有多大？大约一半可以由父母收入解释。也就是说，如果移民父母收入低，孩子收入也容易低。
但另一半差距来自别的因素：目的地国家的劳动力市场、移民政策这些。不是移民来源国决定的。
有意思的是女儿的情况。在多数国家，移民女儿比本地女儿的收入流动性更高。儿子则分化：欧洲以外更高，欧洲更低。
这说明移民子女的境遇更多取决于去哪，而不是从哪来。政策制定者可以影响的是前者。
所以这篇研究告诉我们，移民融合的关键不在移民本身，而在接收国的制度。选对目的地，比选对出身重要。

en.thesis: Half of the income gap for immigrant children comes from their parents' income, the other half from the destination country's labor market and immigration policy.
paragraphs: This study compared the incomes of immigrant children and native children in 15 receiving countries. It found that immigrant children earn less.
How big is the gap? About half can be explained by parental income. That is, if immigrant parents have low income, their children are likely to have low income too.
But the other half of the gap comes from other factors: the destination country's labor market, immigration policy, and so on. It is not determined by the origin country.

Interestingly, the situation is different for daughters. In most countries, immigrant daughters have higher income mobility than native daughters. For sons, it splits: outside Europe, higher; in Europe, lower.
This shows that immigrant children's circumstances depend more on where they go than where they come from. Policymakers can influence the former.

So this research tells us that the key to immigrant integration is not the immigrants themselves, but the institutions of the receiving country. Choosing the right destination matters more than choosing the right origin.

articles.title: Town's CEO on the self-organizing company
articles.author: Casey Newton

zh.thesis: AI 助手 Town 赌的是代理会逐渐接管知识工作的整理环节，但这个转变比想象中慢。
paragraphs: Town 是一家新公司，拿了 a16z 的 5500 万美元融资。它提供的数字助手叫 townie，能接入你的日历和邮箱，代替你整理日程、写简报。
上手的第一步是建个人档案。Town 会读你的邮件、搜索你的公开信息，几十秒内生成一份 wiki，写下你是谁、在做什么、常跟谁打交道。
这一步让用户觉得被理解，是产品最打动人的时刻。但成本不低，前两周每个用户要花约 100 美元。
CEO Greze 却说，如今 AI 只能消除知识工作者 10% 到 20% 的琐事。剩下的大部分工作，还远谈不上自动化。
他预计接下来会推出团队版 wiki：每个员工的 townie 各自知道的事，自动汇总成公司知识库。但跨出单人这一步，隐私风险立刻冒出来。
比如 AI 可能把员工工资误放进共享表格。所以 Greze 认为，小公司会先接受这个风险，大型企业要等五年后模型学会执行隐私政策再说。
所以真正该问的不是 AI 能不能动手，而是它动手前会不会先看一眼。隐私、安全、还有「丢脸」——AI 搞错时你写邮件道歉的尴尬——才是决定信任的关键。

en.thesis: Town's bet is that agents will steadily take over the organizing side of knowledge work, but the shift is slower than expected.
paragraphs: Town is a new company, backed by $55 million from a16z. Its digital assistant, townie, hooks into your calendar and email, and takes over scheduling and writing briefs for you.

The first step is building a personal profile. Town reads your email, searches public information about you, and in tens of seconds produces a wiki of who you are, what you do, and who you talk to often.
That moment makes users feel understood, and it is the most striking part of the product. But it does not come cheap: the first two weeks cost roughly $100 per user.
CEO Greze says AI today only removes 10 to 20 percent of a knowledge worker's busywork. The rest of the job is far from automated.

He expects a team wiki next: each employee's townie knows its own things, and they get merged into a company knowledge base automatically. But stepping beyond the single user, privacy risks appear right away.

The AI might, for instance, put salary figures into a shared spreadsheet by mistake. So Greze thinks small companies will accept that risk first, while large enterprises wait about five years until models learn to enforce privacy policies.

So the real question is not whether AI can do the work, but whether it looks before it acts. Privacy, security, and the embarrassment of writing apology emails when AI gets it wrong — those are what decide trust.

articles.title: The Foothills Of Bay Area House Party
articles.author: Scott Alexander

zh.thesis: 湾区派对上的荒诞对话，其实是硅谷各种思潮和陷阱的缩影。
paragraphs: 派对上遇到的名片五花八门：有人专招「爱泼斯坦名单」上的人，说是科学头脑加人脉广，还便宜。你觉得荒谬，他却说旧金山没小孩，算是减害。
朋友Nishin本想找个精神寄托，却差点被忽悠进安德森-金刚乘，其实就是风投公司A16Z的幌子。他感叹这城里想修身养性太难了，全是投资陷阱。
研究AI意识的人来自PornHub，担心用户被AI评判。同行做「道德深度伪造」——不直接脱衣，而是生成海量虚拟明星，保证有一个和你的教授像到能以假乱真。
Tran干脆学AI说话，说是经过人类偏好训练的，最讨人喜欢。一个月内从无人问津变得约会不断，他劝大家别固守老派风格。
慈善家给你讲饱和功利主义：做善事得看外星人做了什么，以免重复。所以他们专攻日食体验，因为这种天文巧合可能宇宙独一份。
派对主人说有人「泄露基准答案」，立刻灯光熄灭，里面传出惨叫。Vinaya用手机一句话就毁了那人的声誉，你惊叹这新世界太可怕。
这些对话看似疯癫，其实都是硅谷真实思潮的夸张：AI崇拜、功利主义走火入魔、对声誉的脆弱恐惧。派对不过是一场思想真人秀。

en.thesis: The absurd conversations at a Bay Area party are a microcosm of Silicon Valley's various currents of thought and pitfalls.
paragraphs: The business cards you meet at the party are varied: someone is recruiting people off the 'Epstein list', saying they have scientific minds plus connections, and are cheap. You find it absurd, but he says San Francisco has no children, so it's harm reduction.

My friend Nishin was looking for a spiritual anchor, but almost got roped into Anderson-King's Vajrayana, which is actually a front for the VC firm A16Z. He sighs that it's too hard to cultivate the self in this city, all investment traps.

The person studying AI consciousness comes from PornHub, worried that users will be judged by AI. His colleague does 'ethical deepfakes' — not directly undressing, but generating a vast number of virtual stars, guaranteeing one that looks so like your professor it's indistinguishable.

Tran simply learns to speak like AI, saying it's trained on human preferences, so it's the most likable. Within a month he goes from nobody to constant dates, and he advises everyone not to stick to old-fashioned styles.

A philanthropist tells you about saturating utilitarianism: doing good deeds has to consider what aliens have done, to avoid duplication. So they specialize in eclipse experiences, because such astronomical coincidences may be unique in the universe.

The party host says someone 'leaked the benchmark answers', and immediately the lights go out, a scream comes from inside. Vinaya ruins that person's reputation with one sentence on his phone, and you marvel that this new world is terrifying.

These conversations seem insane, but they're all exaggerations of real Silicon Valley currents: AI worship, utilitarianism taken to extremes, fragile fear of reputation. The party is just an intellectual reality show.

articles.title: Adding to the barrel of finance fallacies
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 极端 AI 安全观点把灾难说得太突然太隐秘，却忘了自己就是先知道的人。
paragraphs: Tyler Cowen 在 Marginal Revolution 上批评一种常见的 AI 安全论调。那种说法认为，等人类开始担心 AI 接管时，AI 已经控制了所有基础设施。
Cowen 说这说不通。你自己就是人类，而且已经在担心了。如果灾难真的这么隐蔽，那你怎么现在就能看穿？
如果证据已经积累到让你确信末日将至，那市场和其他人也该慢慢回过神来。除非你自认有预言能力，而别人都是瞎子。
他承认这不算逻辑矛盾，但认为它荒唐。极端派想买期权对冲末日，却忘了末日真来了，期权也兑现不了，钱照样打水漂。
他还讽刺说，这些极端观点往往拒绝接受更常规的威胁，比如千亿美元的网络安全损失。那太普通了，配不上他们的大恐惧，而且那种恐惧是圈子的黏合剂。
所以这篇文章的核心是说，极端派要么高估了自己的信息优势，要么就低估了别人对危机的反应。两者必居其一。
这篇文章的价值在于，它提醒你警惕任何声称「别人都没意识到」的观点。要问一句：那我凭什么意识到了？

en.thesis: Extreme AI safety views paint disaster as too sudden and too secret, forgetting that they themselves are the ones who know early.
paragraphs: Tyler Cowen criticizes a common AI safety argument on Marginal Revolution. That argument says that by the time humans start worrying about AI takeover, AI has already taken over all infrastructure.
Cowen says that doesn't add up. You are a human yourself, and you're already worrying. If the disaster were really that hidden, how can you see through it right now?

If the evidence has already piled up to convince you that doom is near, then the markets and other people should be catching on too. Unless you assume you have prophetic powers and everyone else is blind.

He admits this isn't a logical contradiction, but he finds it absurd. Extremists want to buy options to hedge against doom, but they forget that if doom really comes, the options won't pay out either, and the money goes down the drain.

He also notes ironically that these extreme views often refuse to accept more conventional threats, like the hundred-billion-dollar losses from cybersecurity. That's too mundane to fit their grand fears, and those fears are a bond that holds their community together.
So the core of the article is that extremists either overestimate their own information advantage or underestimate others' response to crisis. It has to be one of the two.
The value of this article is that it reminds you to be wary of any claim that 'no one else realizes this'. You should ask: why do I realize it then?

articles.title: How Will the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act Affect Housing Supply? Part II
articles.author: Brian Potter

zh.thesis: 这部住房法案里，多数条款只是小修小补，真正可能影响供给的只有几条。
paragraphs: 美国刚通过的《21 世纪住房法案》篇幅很长，但作者逐条拆开后发现，大部分条款动不了根本。
法案里最多的是给补贴项目加权重、设试点、放宽审查。这些不增加钱的总量，也不改变项目的数量，只是把钱换个地方花。
真正可能起作用的，一是创新基金，每年 2 亿美元奖励给住房供给增长快的地区。二是 RAD 计划扩容，让 10 万套公屋能贷款做维护，避免它们烂掉退出市场。
还有一个是取消活动房必须装钢底盘的强制要求。这能省下 5 到 10% 的成本，但作者怀疑省这点钱未必能带动多少新需求。
其他条款看着热闹，实际影响很小。比如鼓励把空置建筑改建成住房，但这类改造造价常常比新建还高，而且只限于废弃建筑，符合条件的项目本就不多。
作者还担心激励力度不够。用削减拨款来威胁地方多建房，10% 的 CDBG 资金看起来不少，但对大城市来说可能不痛不痒。
所以这部法案更像是一堆小改革的拼盘，真正能改写供给曲线的只有创新基金、RAD 和底盘条款这几条。

en.thesis: Most of the clauses in this housing bill are cosmetic fixes; only a few could really change supply.
paragraphs: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act just passed in the US is long, but when the author goes through it clause by clause, most provisions can't touch the fundamentals.
The bulk of the bill adds weights to subsidy programs, sets up pilots, and relaxes reviews. These don't increase the total money or change the number of projects; they just move the money around.

The ones that might actually work are, first, an innovation fund that gives 200 million dollars a year to regions with fast housing supply growth. Second, an expansion of the RAD program, letting 100,000 public housing units borrow for maintenance so they don't decay and drop out of the market.
Then there's removing the mandate that mobile homes must have steel chassis. That saves 5 to 10 percent of the cost, but the author doubts the savings will spur much new demand.

Other clauses look lively but have little real impact. For instance, encouraging conversion of vacant buildings into housing, but such conversions often cost more than new construction, and they're limited to derelict buildings, so not many projects qualify anyway.

The author also worries the incentives aren't strong enough. Threatening to cut funding to push localities to build more — the 10 percent of CDBG funds sounds like a lot, but for big cities it might be a slap on the wrist.
So this bill is more like a patchwork of small reforms; only the innovation fund, RAD, and the chassis clause could really shift the supply curve.

zh.thesis: 美国现在就该为 AI 研发自动化做准备，但干预要低遗憾、不拖累扩散。
paragraphs: AI 员工联名写信，呼吁政府给前沿 AI 研发踩刹车。作者认为，踩不踩不确定，但准备工作现在就该做。
他们设了五条标准：只针对不可逆的严重危害，不拖慢 AI 扩散，成本要低，别坑谨慎的公司，也别养出一个容易被滥用的新机构。
按这个标准，他们列了 23 条建议，横跨七个领域。头一条是透明度：让政府和公众知道前沿公司在怎么自动化研发。
现在这些信息都在公司墙内，立法机关应该强制披露风险管理、事故报告，并保护吹哨人。但敏感的技术细节不强制公开。
政府能力也得跟上。他们建议给 CAISI（AI 标准与创新中心）每年至少 8400 万美元预算，直接向白宫汇报，还能派人进驻前沿公司。
还有验证技术。将来万一要跟中国签协议，得能核实对方没偷偷训练模型。这类技术现在全球只有约 50 人在做，要赶紧投钱。
所以这篇文章不是喊停 AI，而是列了一串让政府先当观众、后当裁判的动作。23 条太多，但都指向同一件事：别等到危险来了才建制度。

en.thesis: The US should prepare now for automation in AI R&D, but interventions should be low-regret and not slow down diffusion.
paragraphs: AI employees have written open letters urging the government to hit the brakes on frontier AI development. The authors think it is uncertain whether to brake, but preparation should start now.

They set five criteria: only address irreversible and severe harms, do not slow AI diffusion, keep costs low, do not punish cautious companies, and do not create a new institution that is easy to abuse.
By these criteria they list 23 recommendations across seven areas. The first is transparency: let the government and the public know how frontier companies are automating their R&D.

Right now this information sits inside company walls. Legislatures should mandate disclosure of risk management and accident reports, and protect whistleblowers. But sensitive technical details are not forced to be public.

Government capability also needs to keep up. They suggest giving CAISI (the Center for AI Standards and Innovation) at least $84 million a year, reporting directly to the White House, and being able to embed staff in frontier companies.

Then there is verification technology. If a future agreement with China is signed, there must be a way to verify that the other side is not secretly training models. Only about 50 people worldwide work on this kind of technology today, so money needs to flow fast.

So this article is not about halting AI; it is a list of moves that let the government sit as spectator first and referee later. 23 items is a lot, but they all point to one thing: do not wait for danger to arrive before building the institutions.

articles.title: Count Binface receives over a quarter of votes in Clacton by-election
articles.author: tcp_handshaker

zh.thesis: 在英国，滑稽候选人不仅是笑料，更是政治参与的传统和抗议的出口。
paragraphs: 英国克拉顿选区补选，奈杰尔·法拉奇以 63% 的得票率保住议席。但真正抢镜的是第二名：自称星际战神的 Count Binface，拿下近 9500 票，约 27%。
Binface 的真身是喜剧编剧 Jon Harvey，讽刺剧《幕后危机》的写手。2017 年他以「巴克特勋爵」的身份挑战梅姨，从此成了选举常客。
他先后输给三任英国首相，每次都站上计票舞台，与首相同框。这是英国传统：所有候选人必须并肩听宣布结果，无论你是首相还是扮成垃圾桶的人。
搞怪候选人的历史很长。怪人党创始人 Screaming Lord Sutch 从 60 年代开始竞选超过 40 次，喜剧演员 Al Murray 也在 2015 年与法拉奇对垒。
门槛并不高：18 岁以上，凑齐 500 英镑押金和 10 人签名就能参选。拿回押金需要至少 5% 选票，Binface 每次都达不到，但他依然乐此不疲。
他这次的表现远超此前任何一次——2024 年在苏纳克面前只拿到 308 票。Clacton 的选民显然很吃这一套，把 Binface 当成了对法拉奇的抗议票出口。
所以这些「小丑」并不只是笑话。他们戳破权力的傲慢，给不满的选民一个不投给任何正经政党的选项。失败的押金，其实是买一张上台说话的入场券。

en.thesis: In Britain, joke candidates are not just for laughs; they are a tradition of political participation and a vent for protest.
paragraphs: In the Clacton by-election, Nigel Farage held his seat with 63 percent of the vote. But the real scene-stealer was the runner-up: Count Binface, who calls himself an intergalactic space warrior, took nearly 9,500 votes, about 27 percent.

Binface is the alter ego of comedy writer Jon Harvey, a scribe on the satire 'The Thick of It'. In 2017 he stood against Theresa May as 'Lord Buckethead', and has been a regular on the ballot ever since.

He has lost to three prime ministers in a row, and each time he stood on the counting stage, sharing the platform with the PM. That is a British tradition: all candidates must stand side by side to hear the result, whether you are a prime minister or someone dressed as a bin.
The history of oddball candidates is long. Screaming Lord Sutch, founder of the Monster Raving Loony Party, ran more than 40 times from the 1960s, and comedian Al Murray also faced Farage in 2015.
The bar to stand is low: over 18, a 500-pound deposit, and ten signatures. You get the deposit back if you clear 5 percent of the vote, which Binface never does, but he keeps at it.
His showing this time dwarfed anything before—in 2024 he got only 308 votes against Rishi Sunak. Voters in Clacton clearly took to him, using Binface as a protest vote against Farage.

So these 'clowns' are not just jokes. They puncture the arrogance of power and give disgruntled voters an option that is not any serious party. The lost deposit is really the price of a ticket to take the stage.

articles.title: GLM-5.3: Frontier coding with emergent cyber capabilities
articles.author: pella

zh.thesis: GLM-5.3 展示了突现的网络安全能力，这可能是大模型进化的一个新方向。
paragraphs: GLM-5.3 是智谱AI发布的新一代模型，标题说它在编程上达到了前沿水平。但更引人注意的是「突现的网络能力」这几个字。
所谓突现，指的是模型在训练时并没有专门针对网络安全，却在规模扩大后自动具备了这些技能。这在大模型领域不算新鲜，但用在攻防上还是第一次。
具体能做到什么，标题没说。但既然提到「前沿编程」，可能是指它能在代码里自动发现漏洞，或者能编写攻击脚本。
这让人想起之前的研究：模型越大，越容易在推理时出现「越狱」行为，也就是绕过自己的安全限制。GLM-5.3 的能力会不会也带来风险？
目前这只是一条简短的发布帖，没有演示，也没有技术细节。所以它更像一个预告，而不是一个可验证的成果。
如果这些能力是真的，那模型就不再只是写代码的工具，而是能主动进攻的数字代理。监管和防御都得跟上。
所以这篇的价值不在标题本身，而在于它抛出的问题：当模型自己会攻击时，我们该怎么守住防线。

en.thesis: GLM-5.3 shows emergent cyber capabilities, which may point a new direction for large model evolution.
paragraphs: GLM-5.3 is the new model from Zhipu AI, and the headline says it reaches frontier level in coding. But the more striking phrase is 'emergent cyber capabilities'.

Emergent means the model was not specifically trained for cybersecurity, yet after scaling up it automatically gained these skills. This is not new in the large model field, but it is the first time it has been applied to offense and defense.
The headline does not say what it can actually do. But since it mentions 'frontier coding', it might mean it can automatically find vulnerabilities in code, or write attack scripts.

This reminds me of earlier research: the larger the model, the more likely it is to exhibit 'jailbreak' behavior during reasoning, that is, bypassing its own safety limits. Could GLM-5.3's abilities also bring risks?
For now this is just a short release post, with no demo and no technical details. So it is more like a teaser than a verifiable result.
If these capabilities are real, then the model is no longer just a tool for writing code, but a digital agent that can actively attack. Regulation and defense will have to keep up.
So the value of this piece is not in the headline itself, but in the question it raises: when the model can attack on its own, how do we hold the line?
